records.source: וּבְהַפִּֽילְכֶ֨ם אֶת־הָאָ֜רֶץ בְּנַחֲלָ֗ה תָּרִימוּ֩ תְרוּמָ֨ה לַיהוָ֥ה׀קֹדֶשׁ֮ מִן־הָאָרֶץ֒ אֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשָׂ֣רָה אָ֑לֶף קֹדֶשׁ־ה֥וּא בְכָל־גְּבוּלָ֖הּ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And when you allot the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a contribution to Yahweh, a holy portion from the land: [the] length twenty-five thousand length and [the] breadth ten thousand; holy it [will be] in all its territory all around.
pieces: When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to set apart a special portion for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a holy portion of the land, {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide. All of it will be holy.

L.1: And when you allot the land as an inheritance, you will lift off a contribution for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a holy portion from the land: [as] length, 25,000 [cubits], and [as] width, 10,000; it [will be] holy throughout its whole territory all around.

R.1: When you divide up the land for the tribes to own, you must set aside a special area for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This holy area must be {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide. All of it will be holy.

decisions.choice: a contribution: land set apart and given to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word *terumah* (see 44:30) names something lifted off from the whole and given to the LORD. Here it is a strip of land taken from the whole country before the tribes receive their shares. Chapter 48 describes it again in full (48:8-22).

decisions.choice: 25,000 long and 10,000 wide: the unit is not given
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the numbers with no unit, here and through chapters 45 and 48. Cubits are usually understood, since verse 2 names cubits for the open land. If reeds were meant, as in 42:16-20, every measure would be six times as long. The measures in feet assume cubits.

decisions.choice: 10,000 wide: the Septuagint reads "20,000"
decisions.reason: The Septuagint has 20,000 for the width. That would take in both the priests' strip and the Levites' strip of verses 3-5, each 10,000 wide. The Hebrew 10,000 describes the holy portion of the priests (verse 3). The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: allot the land: divide it by lot
decisions.reason: The verb means to make the lot fall. The land was to be divided by lot, as in Joshua 14:2.

decisions.choice: contribution (L); special portion (B); special area (R)
decisions.reason: The same choice is used for *terumah* as land in chapters 45 and 48. Literal keeps the word's sense of a gift set apart.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}}; {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Worked on the long cubit of 40:5, with the cubits as the alternative. Literal supplies [cubits] (m2).

records.heading: The holy portion of the land

records.source: יִהְיֶ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ אֶל־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת בַּחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת מְרֻבָּ֣ע סָבִ֑יב וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה מִגְרָ֥שׁ ל֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: Of this there will be for the holy place five hundred by five hundred, square all around, and fifty cubits open land for it all around.
pieces: Of this area, a square {{units:about 880 feet|500 cubits}} on each side is to be for the sanctuary, with {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} of open land around it.

L.2: Of this, a square 500 by 500 [cubits] all around will be for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open land around it.

R.2: In this area there must be a square {{units:about 880 feet|500 cubits}} on each side for the temple. Around it there must be an open space {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: 500 by 500: the temple area of 42:15-20
decisions.reason: The square for the sanctuary has the same measure as the walled temple area of 42:20. The measure here is in cubits (see 42:16).

decisions.choice: open land: land around a town kept clear, for pasture or as a buffer
decisions.reason: The word is used for the pasturelands around the Levites' towns (Numbers 35:2-5). Here a strip of open land separates the holy area from everything around it.

decisions.choice: open land (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same English is used for this word in 48:15 and 48:17.

records.source: וּמִן־הַמִּדָּ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ תָּמ֔וֹד אֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְרֹ֖חַב עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים וּבֽוֹ־יִהְיֶ֥ה הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And from this measured [area] you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand, and in it will be the sanctuary, most holy.
pieces: In the area you measure, you are to mark off a section {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide. The sanctuary, the most holy place, will be in it.

L.3: And from this measured area you will measure a length of 25,000 and a width of 10,000, and in it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.

R.3: In the holy area, measure off a section {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide. The temple, the most holy place, will be in this section.

decisions.choice: from this measured area: the part of the holy portion given to the priests
decisions.reason: Verses 3-5 divide the holy portion. The strip described here, with the sanctuary in it, is for the priests (verse 4); a second strip of the same size is for the Levites (verse 5).

decisions.choice: most holy: the sanctuary, the holiest part of the land
decisions.reason: The phrase is "holy of holies", used of the inner room (41:4) and of the whole temple area (43:12).

records.source: קֹ֣דֶשׁ מִן־הָאָ֜רֶץ ה֗וּא לַכֹּ֨הֲנִ֜ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֤י הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה הַקְּרֵבִ֖ים לְשָׁרֵ֣ת אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם מָקוֹם֙ לְבָ֣תִּ֔ים וּמִקְדָּ֖שׁ לַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: It [is] a holy portion from the land; for the priests, ministers of the sanctuary, it will be, who come near to serve Yahweh; and it will be for them a place for houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
pieces: This holy portion of the land is to belong to the priests who serve in the sanctuary, who come near to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will be a place for their houses and a holy area for the sanctuary.

L.4: It [is] a holy portion of the land; it will belong to the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who approach to minister to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and it will be for them a place for houses and a holy area for the sanctuary.

R.4: This holy part of the land will belong to the priests who serve in the temple and come near {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will have their homes there, and the temple will be there too.

decisions.choice: a place for houses: the priests receive no inheritance, only land to live on
decisions.reason: This fits 44:28: the LORD is the priests' inheritance, so they own no tribal land. They are given space for their houses around the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds the pronoun for the LORD.

records.source: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים רֹ֑חַב וְֽהָיָ֡ה לַלְוִיִּם֩ מְשָׁרְתֵ֨י הַבַּ֧יִת לָהֶ֛ם לַאֲחֻזָּ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים לְשָׁכֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And twenty-five thousand length and ten thousand breadth will be for the Levites, ministers of the house, for them as a holding, twenty rooms.
pieces: Another area {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide is to belong to the Levites who serve in the temple, as their property: twenty rooms.

L.5: And [an area] 25,000 long and 10,000 wide will be for the Levites, the ministers of the house, as their holding: twenty chambers.

R.5: Another area {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long and {{units:about 3 1/3 miles|10,000 cubits}} wide will belong to the Levites who serve in the temple. It will be their property, with twenty rooms.

decisions.choice: twenty rooms: the Septuagint reads "cities to live in"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "twenty rooms" (or "chambers") is hard to fit with a strip of land. The Septuagint reads "cities to dwell in", which differs from the Hebrew by a few letters; the Levites in the law had towns to live in (Numbers 35:2). The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: a holding: land held as one's own
decisions.reason: The word *'achuzzah* means land that is held, a possession.

decisions.choice: holding (L); property (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same choice is used for *'achuzzah* in chapters 45-48.

records.source: וַאֲחֻזַּ֨ת הָעִ֜יר תִּתְּנ֗וּ חֲמֵ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ רֹ֔חַב וְאֹ֗רֶךְ חֲמִשָּׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף לְעֻמַּ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ לְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And [as the] holding of the city you will give five thousand breadth and length twenty-five thousand, alongside [the] holy contribution; for all [the] house of Israel it will be.
pieces: As the city's property you are to assign an area {{units:about 1 2/3 miles|5,000 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long, next to the holy portion. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.

L.6: And as the holding of the city you will give [an area] 5,000 wide and 25,000 long, alongside the holy contribution; it will belong to the whole house of Israel.

R.6: Next to the holy area, set aside land for the city. It must be {{units:about 1 2/3 miles|5,000 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 8 1/4 miles|25,000 cubits}} long. It will belong to all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: for the whole house of Israel: the city belongs to no single tribe
decisions.reason: Jerusalem had been David's city, taken from the Jebusites and not part of any tribe's land. The new city belongs to all Israel, and 48:19 says its workers come from all the tribes.

decisions.choice: holy contribution (L); holy portion (B); holy area (R)
decisions.reason: The terms for *terumat haqqodesh* in chapters 45 and 48.

records.source: וְלַנָּשִׂ֡יא מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּה֩ לִתְרוּמַ֨ת הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ וְלַאֲחֻזַּ֣ת הָעִ֗יר אֶל־פְּנֵ֤י תְרֽוּמַת־הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ וְאֶל־פְּנֵי֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת הָעִ֔יר מִפְּאַת־יָ֣ם יָ֔מָּה וּמִפְּאַת־קֵ֖דְמָה קָדִ֑ימָה וְאֹ֗רֶךְ לְעֻמּוֹת֙ אַחַ֣ד הַחֲלָקִ֔ים מִגְּב֥וּל יָ֖ם אֶל־גְּב֥וּל קָדִֽימָה׃
records.gloss: And for the prince, on this side and on this side of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, to [the] face of the holy contribution and to [the] face of the holding of the city, from [the] west side westward and from [the] east side eastward, and [the] length corresponding to one of the portions, from [the] west border to [the] east border.
pieces: The prince is to have the land on both sides of the holy portion and the city's property, next to the holy portion and the city's property, reaching west from the western side and east from the eastern side, its length matching one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.

L.7: And to the prince [will belong the land] on either side of the holy contribution and the city's holding, alongside the holy contribution and alongside the city's holding, from the west side westward and from the east side eastward, its length matching one of the [tribal] portions, from the western border to the eastern border.

R.7: The ruler will own the land on both sides of the holy area and the city's land. His land will reach west to the Mediterranean Sea and east to the Jordan, the full width of one of the tribes' shares.

decisions.choice: the prince's land: east and west of the central square
decisions.reason: The holy portion and the city's land form a square 25,000 on each side (48:20). The land on either side of it, east and west, as far as the borders of the country, belongs to the prince (48:21-22). The western border is the Mediterranean and the eastern the Jordan (47:18-20).

decisions.choice: west to the Mediterranean Sea and east to the Jordan (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the borders given in 47:18-20.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:3.

records.source: לָאָ֛רֶץ יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ לַֽאֲחֻזָּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹא־יוֹנ֨וּ ע֤וֹד נְשִׂיאַי֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְהָאָ֛רֶץ יִתְּנ֥וּ לְבֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְשִׁבְטֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Of the land it will be his for a holding in Israel; and my princes will no longer oppress my people, and the land they will give to [the] house of Israel according to their tribes.
pieces: This land is to be his property in Israel. Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} princes will no longer oppress {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, but will let the house of Israel have the land according to their tribes.

L.8: It will be his land as a holding in Israel; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} princes will oppress {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people no more, but the land they will give to the house of Israel by their tribes.

R.8: This land will be the ruler's property in Israel. Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulers will no longer mistreat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. They will let the people of Israel have the rest of the land, tribe by tribe.

decisions.choice: my princes will no longer oppress my people: the prince's land removes the reason for seizing others' land
decisions.reason: The kings of Israel and Judah had taken land and labor from the people (1 Samuel 8:14; 1 Kings 21; Jeremiah 22:13-17). With land of his own, the prince has no need to take theirs (46:18).

decisions.choice: my princes (L, B); my rulers (R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:3.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה רַב־לָכֶם֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חָמָ֤ס וָשֹׁד֙ הָסִ֔ירוּ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה עֲשׂ֑וּ הָרִ֤ימוּ גְרֻשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ מֵעַ֣ל עַמִּ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Enough for you, princes of Israel! Violence and destruction remove, and justice and righteousness do; take away your evictions from my people, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Enough, princes of Israel! Put an end to violence and destruction, and do what is just and right. Stop driving {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people off their land, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.9: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Enough, princes of Israel! Put away violence and destruction, and do justice and righteousness; stop your evictions of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.9: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You rulers of Israel have done enough wrong! Stop your violence and robbery. Do what is fair and right. Stop forcing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people off their land, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your evictions: driving people off their land
decisions.reason: The word means expulsion. It describes the seizing of family land by the powerful, which the law forbade (Leviticus 25:23; Micah 2:2; Isaiah 5:8).

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: the standard for kings
decisions.reason: The pair describes the right rule of a king (2 Samuel 8:15; Jeremiah 22:3, 15; 23:5).

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness (L); what is just and right (B); what is fair and right (R)
decisions.reason: Readable follows the Amos table for this pair ("what is right").

decisions.choice: driving my people off their land (B); forcing my people off their land (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evictions". Balanced and Readable say what was done (m1).

records.heading: Honest rulers and honest measures

records.source: מֹֽאזְנֵי־צֶ֧דֶק וְאֵֽיפַת־צֶ֛דֶק וּבַת־צֶ֖דֶק יְהִ֥י לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Balances of righteousness and an ephah of righteousness and a bath of righteousness let there be for you.
pieces: You are to use honest scales, an honest ephah and an honest bath.

L.10: You will have honest scales, an honest ephah and an honest bath.

R.10: You must use honest scales and honest measures for grain and for liquids.

decisions.choice: the ephah and the bath: the standard measures for grain and for liquids
decisions.reason: The ephah measured dry goods such as flour and grain; the bath measured liquids such as oil and wine. Dishonest measures were a common way of cheating (Amos 8:5; Micah 6:10-11; Leviticus 19:35-36).

decisions.choice: of righteousness: honest, true
decisions.reason: The phrase "balances of righteousness" means scales that weigh truly (Leviticus 19:36).

decisions.choice: an ephah, a bath (L, B); measures for grain and for liquids (R)
decisions.reason: Here the measures themselves are the subject, so Literal and Balanced keep their names without a modern equivalent. Readable says what they measured; their size is given in verse 11.

records.source: הָאֵיפָ֣ה וְהַבַּ֗ת תֹּ֤כֶן אֶחָד֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה לָשֵׂ֕את מַעְשַׂ֥ר הַחֹ֖מֶר הַבָּ֑ת וַעֲשִׂירִ֤ת הַחֹ֨מֶר֙ הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה אֶל־הַחֹ֖מֶר יִהְיֶ֥ה מַתְכֻּנְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: The ephah and the bath one measure will be, to contain a tenth of the homer the bath, and a tenth of the homer the ephah; according to the homer will be its measure.
pieces: The ephah and the bath are to be the same size, the bath holding {{units:about 6 gallons|a tenth of a homer}} and the ephah {{units:about 6 gallons|a tenth of a homer}}. The homer is to be the standard for both.

L.11: The ephah and the bath will be one measure, the bath holding a tenth of the homer, and the ephah a tenth of the homer; its measure will be according to the homer.

R.11: The measure for grain and the measure for liquids must be the same size. Each one must hold {{units:about 6 gallons|a tenth of a homer}}. The homer is the standard for both.

decisions.choice: the ephah and the bath of one size: about 6 gallons each
decisions.reason: The verse makes the dry measure (ephah) and the liquid measure (bath) equal, each a tenth of the homer. Ancient measures varied from place to place and over time, and modern estimates differ widely: the bath is reckoned at about 6 gallons (22 liters), and the ephah at anything from about half a bushel to about two-thirds of a bushel. The published books of this translation give an ephah as about 20 quarts; in Ezekiel, where the text sets the two measures equal, both are given as about 6 gallons, and a homer as ten of them (about 60 gallons, or about 6 bushels of grain).

decisions.choice: the homer: the largest measure, ten ephahs or ten baths
decisions.reason: The name may mean "a donkey load". It was the same as the kor (verse 14).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 6 gallons|a tenth of a homer}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 45-46 the ephah and the bath are both given as about 6 gallons, since the text sets them equal (m1).

decisions.choice: the measure for grain and the measure for liquids (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

records.source: וְהַשֶּׁ֖קֶל עֶשְׂרִ֣ים גֵּרָ֑ה עֶשְׂרִ֨ים שְׁקָלִ֜ים חֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים עֲשָׂרָ֤ה וַחֲמִשָּׁה֙ שֶׁ֔קֶל הַמָּנֶ֖ה יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the shekel [will be] twenty gerahs; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, fifteen shekels the mina will be for you.
pieces: The shekel is to be twenty gerahs. Your mina is to be {{units:about 8 ounces|twenty shekels}} plus {{units:about 10 ounces|twenty-five shekels}} plus {{units:about 6 ounces|fifteen shekels}}.

L.12: And the shekel will be twenty gerahs; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels [and] fifteen shekels will be your mina.

R.12: A shekel must weigh twenty gerahs. A mina must weigh {{units:about 1 1/2 pounds|sixty shekels}}: twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels.

decisions.choice: the shekel and the gerah: weights
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight of silver of about two-fifths of an ounce (11 grams); the gerah was a twentieth of it. The same definition is given in Exodus 30:13 and Leviticus 27:25.

decisions.choice: twenty, twenty-five and fifteen shekels make the mina: sixty shekels
decisions.reason: The three amounts add up to sixty, so the mina is to be sixty shekels, about 1 1/2 pounds. The odd way of stating it may name three weights in use, or may be meant to fix the total. Elsewhere a mina could be fifty shekels.

decisions.choice: the Septuagint has different figures
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads differently here, with a mina of fifty shekels. The translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the shekel amounts in ounces (B); the mina as about 1 1/2 pounds (R)
decisions.reason: The definition "the shekel is twenty gerahs" is kept as it stands at every level, as in Leviticus 27:25. Balanced gives each amount in ounces (as 4:10). Readable states the total of sixty shekels (m2) and gives its weight.

records.source: זֹ֥את הַתְּרוּמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֑ימוּ שִׁשִּׁ֤ית הָֽאֵיפָה֙ מֵחֹ֣מֶר הַֽחִטִּ֔ים וְשִׁשִּׁיתֶם֙ הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה מֵחֹ֖מֶר הַשְּׂעֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: This [is] the contribution which you will offer: a sixth of the ephah from the homer of the wheat, and you will give a sixth of the ephah from [the] homer of the barley.
pieces: This is the special offering you are to give: {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}} from every {{units:6 bushels|homer}} of wheat, and {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}} from every {{units:6 bushels|homer}} of barley.

L.13: This [is] the contribution that you will offer: a sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and you will give a sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley,

R.13: This is the special offering you must give: from every {{units:6 bushels|homer}} of wheat or barley, give {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}}.

decisions.choice: a sixth of an ephah from a homer: one part in sixty
decisions.reason: A homer is ten ephahs, so a sixth of an ephah is a sixtieth of the grain. These gifts go to the prince for the offerings (verses 16-17).

decisions.choice: the contribution: the people's gift for the offerings
decisions.reason: The same word as the land of verse 1, here used for gifts of produce (as 44:30).

decisions.choice: contribution (L); special offering (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here *terumah* is a gift of produce, as in 44:30.

decisions.choice: {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}}; {{units:6 bushels|homer}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: On the ephah of about 6 gallons (verse 11); the homer of grain is given as about 6 bushels (see verse 11).

records.source: וְחֹ֨ק הַשֶּׁ֜מֶן הַבַּ֣ת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶן מַעְשַׂ֤ר הַבַּת֙ מִן־הַכֹּ֔ר עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַבַּתִּ֖ים חֹ֑מֶר כִּֽי־עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הַבַּתִּ֖ים חֹֽמֶר׃
records.gloss: And the portion of the oil, the bath of the oil, a tenth of the bath from the kor, ten baths [are] a homer, for ten baths [are] a homer.
pieces: The portion of oil, measured by the bath, is to be {{units:about 2 1/2 quarts|a tenth of a bath}} from every {{units:60 gallons|kor}} (a kor is ten baths, the same as a homer, for ten baths make a homer).

L.14: and the portion of oil, measured by the bath, a tenth of a bath from each kor (ten baths [are] a homer, for ten baths [are] a homer);

R.14: Of olive oil, give {{units:about 2 1/2 quarts|a tenth of a bath}} from every {{units:60 gallons|kor}}. A kor holds ten baths, the same as a homer.

decisions.choice: the kor: a large measure, the same as the homer
decisions.reason: The kor is used for large amounts of grain and oil (1 Kings 5:2, 25). It held ten baths, the same as a homer.

decisions.choice: ten baths are a homer, for ten baths are a homer: a repeated note
decisions.reason: The phrase is said twice, perhaps for emphasis, perhaps by a copyist's slip. One part in a hundred of the oil is to be given.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 2 1/2 quarts|a tenth of a bath}}; {{units:60 gallons|kor}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: On the bath of about 6 gallons (verse 11).

records.source: וְשֶׂה־אַחַ֨ת מִן־הַצֹּ֤אן מִן־הַמָּאתַ֨יִם֙ מִמַּשְׁקֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְמִנְחָ֖ה וּלְעוֹלָ֣ה וְלִשְׁלָמִ֑ים לְכַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And one sheep from the flock, from the two hundred, from [the] well-watered [land] of Israel, for grain offering and for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to make atonement for them, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: and one sheep out of every 200 from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These will be used for grain offerings, burnt offerings and peace offerings, to make atonement on the people's behalf, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: and one sheep from the flock out of every 200, from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for the grain offering, the burnt offering and the peace offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: Give one sheep out of every 200 from the good pastures of Israel. These gifts will be used for the grain offerings, the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the well-watered land of Israel: the good pastures
decisions.reason: The word means a watered place, a place where flocks drink. Some read it as "the families of Israel", from a similar word in the Septuagint.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for them: the offerings restore the people's relationship with the LORD
decisions.reason: Not only the sin offering but all the offerings, brought on behalf of the whole people, cover their sin and keep them acceptable to the LORD (verse 17).

records.source: כֹּ֚ל הָעָ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ יִהְי֖וּ אֶל־הַתְּרוּמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את לַנָּשִׂ֖יא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: All the people of the land will [give] to this contribution for the prince in Israel.
pieces: All the people of the land are to give this special offering to the prince in Israel.

L.16: All the people of the land will [give] this contribution to the prince in Israel.

R.16: All the people of the land must give these special offerings to the ruler of Israel.

decisions.choice: will be to this contribution: they will give it to the prince
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "will be to this contribution"; the people are to share in it, giving it to the prince, who then provides the offerings (verse 17).

decisions.choice: [give] (L); give (B, R)
decisions.reason: Supplied from the context (m1).

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:3.

records.source: וְעַֽל־הַנָּשִׂ֣יא יִהְיֶ֗ה הָעוֹל֣וֹת וְהַמִּנְחָה֮ וְהַנֵּסֶךְ֒ בַּחַגִּ֤ים וּבֶחֳדָשִׁים֙ וּבַשַּׁבָּת֔וֹת בְּכָֽל־מוֹעֲדֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֽוּא־יַעֲשֶׂ֞ה אֶת־הַחַטָּ֣את וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֗ה וְאֶת־הָֽעוֹלָה֙ וְאֶת־הַשְּׁלָמִ֔ים לְכַפֵּ֖ר בְּעַ֥ד בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And on the prince will be the burnt offerings and the grain offering and the drink offering, at festivals and at new moons and on Sabbaths, at all [the] appointed feasts of [the] house of Israel; he will provide the sin offering and the grain offering and the burnt offering and the peace offerings, to make atonement for [the] house of Israel.
pieces: The prince is to be responsible for the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the drink offerings at the festivals, the new moons and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed festivals of the house of Israel. He is to supply the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings and peace offerings that make atonement for the house of Israel.

L.17: And it will be the prince's duty [to provide] the burnt offerings, the grain offering and the drink offering, at the festivals, the new moons and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. It is he who will provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering and the peace offerings, to make atonement on behalf of the house of Israel.

R.17: The ruler must provide the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the drink offerings for the festivals, for the first day of each month and for the Sabbath days. He must provide them for all the special days of the people of Israel. He must provide the sin offerings, the grain offerings, the burnt offerings and the peace offerings to make atonement for the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: festivals, new moons and Sabbaths: Israel's calendar of worship
decisions.reason: The festivals are the three great pilgrim feasts; the new moon was the first day of each month (Numbers 28:11); the Sabbath was the seventh day. Numbers 28-29 sets out the offerings for each.

decisions.choice: he will provide: the prince leads the people's worship
decisions.reason: The kings of Judah had provided offerings (2 Chronicles 31:3). The prince does not serve as priest; he supplies the offerings, and the priests offer them (46:2).

decisions.choice: the first day of each month (R)
decisions.reason: As Numbers 28:11 at Readable.

records.source: כֹּה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ תִּקַּ֥ח פַּר־בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר תָּמִ֑ים וְחִטֵּאתָ֖ אֶת־הַמִּקְדָּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: In the first [month], on [the] first of the month, you will take a bull, a young one of [the] herd, unblemished, and you will cleanse the sanctuary.
pieces: the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: In the first month, on its first day, you are to take a young bull without defect and purify the sanctuary.

L.18: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: In the first [month], on the first [day] of the month, you will take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.

R.18: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Each year, on the first day of the first month, take a young bull that has nothing wrong with it. Use it to make the temple pure.

decisions.choice: the first day of the first month: the new year in spring
decisions.reason: The first month (later called Nisan) falls in March-April. Ezekiel gives a yearly purification of the sanctuary at the new year, which is not in the law of Moses; the law's Day of Atonement was in the seventh month (Leviticus 16:29).

decisions.choice: cleanse the sanctuary: purify it from sin
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 43:20, 22.

records.heading: The yearly festivals

records.source: וְלָקַ֨ח הַכֹּהֵ֜ן מִדַּ֣ם הַחַטָּ֗את וְנָתַן֙ אֶל־מְזוּזַ֣ת הַבַּ֔יִת וְאֶל־אַרְבַּ֛ע פִּנּ֥וֹת הָעֲזָרָ֖ה לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְעַ֨ל־מְזוּזַ֔ת שַׁ֖עַר הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃
records.gloss: And the priest will take some of [the] blood of the sin offering and put [it] on [the] doorpost of the house and on [the] four corners of the ledge of the altar and on [the] doorpost of [the] gate of the court the inner.
pieces: The priest is to take some blood from the sin offering and smear it on the temple doorposts, on the four corners of the altar's upper ledge and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.

L.19: And the priest will take from the blood of the sin offering and set [it] on the doorposts of the house, and on the four corners of the altar's ledge, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.

R.19: The priest must take some blood from the sin offering. He must smear it on the temple doorposts, on the four corners of the upper ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner courtyard.

decisions.choice: blood on the doorposts: purifying the house
decisions.reason: The blood marks the places of entry, as the Passover blood was put on the doorposts (Exodus 12:7). Here it purifies the temple, the altar and the court.

decisions.choice: ledge (all levels)
decisions.reason: As in 43:14.

records.source: וְכֵ֤ן תַּֽעֲשֶׂה֙ בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה בַחֹ֔דֶשׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ שֹׁגֶ֖ה וּמִפֶּ֑תִי וְכִפַּרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And so you will do on the seventh [day] of the month, for anyone who errs and for the simple; and you will make atonement for the house.
pieces: You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins by mistake or without knowing it. In this way you will make atonement for the temple.

L.20: And you will do the same on the seventh [day] of the month for anyone who has sinned unintentionally or through ignorance; so you will make atonement for the house.

R.20: On the seventh day of the month, do the same thing for anyone who has sinned by accident or without knowing it. In this way you will make atonement for the temple.

decisions.choice: on the seventh of the month: the Septuagint reads "in the seventh month, on the first of the month"
alternatives: in the seventh month, on the first of the month
decisions.reason: The Septuagint makes this a second rite, half a year later, in the seventh month. The Hebrew has it a week after the first. The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: for anyone who errs and for the simple: sins done without intent
decisions.reason: The law provided sin offerings for sins done by mistake or in ignorance (Leviticus 4:2, 13; Numbers 15:22-29). The simple person is one who does not know better.

records.source: בָּ֠רִאשׁוֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַפָּ֑סַח חָ֕ג שְׁבֻע֣וֹת יָמִ֔ים מַצּ֖וֹת יֵאָכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: In the first [month], on [the] fourteenth day of the month, the Passover will be for you, a festival of weeks of days; unleavened bread will be eaten.
pieces: On the fourteenth day of the first month you are to celebrate the Passover, a festival lasting seven days, during which bread made without yeast is to be eaten.

L.21: In the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month, you will have the Passover, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread will be eaten.

R.21: On the fourteenth day of the first month, you must celebrate the Passover. It is a festival that lasts seven days. During that time you must eat bread made without yeast.

decisions.choice: a festival of weeks of days: usually read "a festival of seven days"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "a festival of weeks of days". By a change of vowels it reads "a festival of seven days", which is the length of the feast of unleavened bread in the law (Exodus 12:15; Leviticus 23:6) and fits verse 23. The ancient versions read it so.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the feast of Israel's deliverance from Egypt
decisions.reason: Exodus 12 and Leviticus 23:5-8. Ezekiel joins the Passover and the seven days of unleavened bread, as Deuteronomy 16:1-8 does.

decisions.choice: unleavened bread (L); bread made without yeast (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what unleavened bread is.

records.source: וְעָשָׂ֤ה הַנָּשִׂיא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא בַּעֲד֕וֹ וּבְעַ֖ד כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ פַּ֖ר חַטָּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And the prince will provide on that day for himself and for all [the] people of the land a bull of sin offering.
pieces: On that day the prince is to provide a young bull as a sin offering on behalf of himself and all the people of the land.

L.22: And on that day the prince will provide for himself and for all the people of the land a young bull for a sin offering.

R.22: On that day the ruler must provide a young bull as a sin offering for himself and for everyone in the land.

decisions.choice: for himself: the prince needs atonement like everyone else
decisions.reason: The prince brings a sin offering for his own sin, as the people do. He is a human ruler, not a divine figure (see 44:3).

records.source: וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת יְמֵֽי־הֶחָ֜ג יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה עוֹלָ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֗ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת פָּ֠רִים וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת אֵילִ֤ים תְּמִימִם֙ לַיּ֔וֹם שִׁבְעַ֖ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְחַטָּ֕את שְׂעִ֥יר עִזִּ֖ים לַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And [the] seven days of the festival he will provide a burnt offering to Yahweh, seven bulls and seven rams unblemished, daily [for] the seven days, and a sin offering, a male goat of goats, daily.
pieces: During the seven days of the festival he is to provide seven young bulls and seven rams without defect as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.

L.23: And during the seven days of the festival he will provide as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} seven young bulls and seven rams without blemish, daily for the seven days, and for a sin offering a male goat daily.

R.23: During each of the seven days of the festival, he must provide seven young bulls and seven rams as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. None of them may have anything wrong with them. He must also provide a male goat each day as a sin offering.

decisions.choice: seven bulls and seven rams: more than the law required
decisions.reason: Numbers 28:19-24 required two bulls, one ram and seven lambs each day of the feast. Ezekiel's offerings are different and larger.

records.source: וּמִנְחָ֗ה אֵיפָ֥ה לַפָּ֛ר וְאֵיפָ֥ה לָאַ֖יִל יַֽעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And a grain offering, an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he will provide, and oil a hin for the ephah.
pieces: He is to provide a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} for each bull and {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} for each ram, together with {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of oil for each ephah.

L.24: And [as] a grain offering, an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he will provide, and a hin of oil for each ephah.

R.24: He must also provide a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} of flour for each bull and each ram, with {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil for each ephah.

decisions.choice: an ephah, a hin: grain and oil with each animal
decisions.reason: A hin was a sixth of a bath, about a gallon. The amounts are much larger than in Numbers 28:20-21, where a bull had three tenths of an ephah of flour.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}}; {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: On the ephah of about 6 gallons (verse 11) and the hin of about a gallon, as published (Ezekiel 4:11).

records.source: בַּשְּׁבִיעִ֡י בַּחֲמִשָּׁה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ בֶּחָ֔ג יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה כָאֵ֖לֶּה שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים כַּֽחַטָּאת֙ כָּעֹלָ֔ה וְכַמִּנְחָ֖ה וְכַשָּֽׁמֶן׃ס
records.gloss: In the seventh [month], on [the] fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he will provide like these [for] the seven days, like the sin offering, like the burnt offering, and like the grain offering, and like the oil.
pieces: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, at the festival, he is to make the same provision for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and oil.

L.25: In the seventh [month], on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he will provide the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering and oil.

R.25: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, at the festival, he must provide the same offerings for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and olive oil.

decisions.choice: the festival in the seventh month: the Festival of Shelters
decisions.reason: The fifteenth day of the seventh month (September-October) began the seven-day Festival of Shelters, or Booths (Leviticus 23:34). It is called simply "the festival", as in 1 Kings 8:2. Ezekiel's calendar names no Festival of Weeks and no Day of Atonement.
